chapter: Rabbit Foot show and show life
title: Rabbit Foot show parades and shrinking band size
summary: On the Rabbit Foot Show he played trombone, paraded daily, and the band shrank from 15 to nine as parading stopped.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Anything else about these shows? Did they ever... Were some of the acts mostly dance acts or did you play overtures? Did you ever play any parades or what all did you do?
Lots of parades. Same fellas get out there. But being in the pit, you might say, at night, we get out and parade in the day.

Well, yes. And, well, the Rabbit Foot Men's show. I worked with them a long time. I was a trombone player with them. Well, we done a lot of parades. At one o'clock in the day, you get out and you parade, I would say, two and a half hours. And you come back in and you'd be ready for six days to hit that first show. Well, that was years back.
How big a band would you have most of these shows?

The Rabbit Foot just carried 15 pieces. 15, right? That's right. Well, as time passed on, he started cutting down, cutting down. You know, as show business began to fade, well, he would cut down and cut down. Well, the last time I was with the Rabbit Foot show, he had nine pieces. And they had cut out the parading, no more parading. We'd just go in the show and start playing around 6.30. We'd play our overture. And then I would say, quarters to seven, the first act comes on. And we'd just play like he was playing in a theater, but no more parading.
